newsitem.title: TURKEY: No plans for Turkish lira parity with dlr - minister.
newsitem.headline: No plans for Turkish lira parity with dlr - minister.

text.p: Turkish State Minister Ufuk Soylemez on Tuesday said there were no plans underway to relaunch the Turkish lira at a rate of one to one against the U.S. dollar, adding conditions were not ready for such a move.

"There's no question of the government having begun technical work on achieving parity between the Turkish lira and the dollar and the government has not taken such a decision," Soylemez, in charge of privatisation and the Treasury, told Reuters by telephone.

Earlier Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan told deputies from his Welfare Party "Work is being carried out in connection with making one Turkish lira equal to one dollar and keeping it steady".
Soylemez, from the conservative wing of the coalition, said controlling inflation and implementing a well organised stability progamme were pre-requisites for such a project.
"From a technical and legal standpoint it would not be possible to initiate such a project until such conditions were in place," he said.

The Turkish lira was quoted at 97,140 per dollar on Tuesday. The lira has lost around 40 percent of its value against the dollar since the start of the year and annual inflation in Turkey is around 80 percent.
